acme-cs: Hey team — our invoice shows ~35k more tokens than our SDK estimator. Payloads are identical AFAICT. Can someone look? We have a minimal repro below.

emma: Sorry about the surprise, thanks for flagging. Can you paste the exact request + response (sanitized) and SDK version?

acme-cs: SDK v0.9.4, here's a minimal curl we used (redacted key):
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{\n    "model": "redwood-chat-1",\n    "messages": [\n      {"role": "system", "content": "You are an assistant."},\n      {"role": "user", "content": "Summarize the following notes..."}\n    ],\n    "max_tokens": 200,\n    "stream": false\n  }'
```

acme-cs: SDK estimator reported ~1.2k tokens for 500 calls. Invoice shows ~36k.

raj: Noted. Two quick possibilities: (1) server-injected messages / tool outputs are billed but client estimator doesn't see injected tokens, (2) function/tool calls that return long outputs after the SDK stopped streaming. Do you have the raw response body (server) including function/tool sections?

acme-cs: We only saved the SDK response — it stops after the final `finish_reason` in the client. How do we capture server-side extra tokens?

sophie: If your request triggers an internal helper (sidecar/tool) that appends content after the model response, those tokens are counted in billing. The client estimator only tokenizes what the client sees; if the server inserts a system note or tool output post-response, it won't be counted by clients. Can you check your model route rules? Any routing to `tooling-proxy`?

acme-cs: Ah — our route had `enable_tracing: true` and an experimental `metadata_enrichment` hook. Might be related.

emma: Can you run this repro with `?include_injected=true` on the API to get the full server payload? If you can't, we can pull logs for the request IDs if you share a sample timestamp/req_id.

acme-cs: Sample req_id: r-2026-02-15-9ab3f. We just enabled debugging on a single call and saw an extra system message appended after completion: `{"role":"system","content":"enriched: source=kb-lookup, tokens=142"}`.

raj: That matches our meter: the extra 142 tokens per call * 250 calls ~= 35.5k. So it's server-injected enrichment tokens. Billing team counts any tokens added by the platform.

sophie: Short-term mitigation: (1) disable `metadata_enrichment` for customer routes, (2) or set enrichment to `summarize: true` which compresses outputs. Long-term: we should add a header/response flag that lists injected token counts so SDKs can surface an "estimated billed tokens" number.

acme-cs: Thanks — disabling enrichment reduced the invoice spike in staging. Can you confirm whether we should expect these injected tokens to be billed going forward? Need this for our internal chargeback.

raj: Yes — any server-generated content (system/tool/sidecar) is billable. We'll mark this ticket as billing-impact. I'm adding a note to docs and opening a small feature request to emit `x-redwood-injected-tokens` in responses.

metering-bot: Ticket created: #INC-3912 (billing) — assigned to raj, notify: eng-ml.

emma: Action items: (1) raj to update billing docs and confirm invoice adjustment window if any, (2) sophie to add response header flag proposal and a short RFC, (3) acme-cs to confirm no other auto-hooks enabled. I'll follow up with timeline. :thumbsup:

sophie: RFC sketch — include `x-rw-injected-tokens: <n>` on responses and a new `include_injected` query param for debugging. Also add a metering event type `injected_token` in backend logs so we can export per-customer. I'll open the PR tomorrow.

acme-cs: Appreciate the quick triage. We'll keep enrichment off for prod for now.

emma: Closing loop after raj confirms doc updates. If customer wants invoice credit review, please DM billing with the affected invoices.

raj: Follow-up: billing will honor adjustment requests within 30 days with clear repro evidence.

acme-cs: Understood — will send the IDs.

emma: Thanks everyone.
